validation.scheme: 4-fold GroupKFold by exchange group (no group split across folds); exact published mean_clipped_structured_brier_v1 metric; all memory/kNN features for labelled rows computed out-of-fold by group (inner 4-fold GroupKFold) so no row ever retrieves from its own exchange

model.architecture: Permutation CRF: pair score = full-rank learned bucket x bucket compatibility matrices (last context segment, previous segment, lattice-successor segment, event-specific last segment; 4 x 378 x 378, L2 1e-3) + 2-layer MLP (64 hidden) over 40 pair features [20 structural/overlap: has_prev/has_succ x outcome_kind, content lengths, word/value/filler overlaps per segment; 12 exact-key memory stats; 8 soft-kNN similarities to true and false pairs from other exchange groups]; exact 24-permutation softmax trained with permutation cross-entropy (full batch Adam, 300 iters); MAP-permutation decoding
model.decoding_rationale: For doubly-stochastic P the row score is clip(1 - ||P - Y||_F^2, 0, 1). Distinct permutation matrices are >= 2 apart, so at most one permutation can receive a positive score for any P; the expected-score-optimal output is the MAP permutation matrix (expected score = its posterior probability). Confirmed on OOF: T=1 0.408 -> T=0.1 0.534 -> MAP 0.547.

constraints.notes: group used only for fold construction. Vocabulary is closed (manifest bucket sizes). Feature standardization, IDF and retrieval memory are fitted on training rows only; test rows are only queried.

experiments.name: E0 starter (as provided)
experiments.result: crashed: pair_in = D_MODEL*4+14+8 = 342 but concatenated pair vector is 422 wide (outcome embedding omitted)
experiments.decision: fixed one line to obtain a baseline

experiments.name: E1 neural set encoder (multi-head attention pooling, prev/last/successor segments, full bilinear, axial row/column attention, 24-perm CE)
experiments.decision: rejected: memorizes training rows by epoch 3 (train CE 0.005) while val NLL explodes; superseded by E2/E3

experiments.name: E2 bilinear permutation CRF + MLP over structural and exact-key memory features
experiments.decision: kept as base: +0.08 over E1 on every fold

experiments.name: E3 E2 + soft kNN pair-retrieval features (TF-IDF bags, similarity to true/false pairs in other groups)
experiments.decision: kept: small but consistent gain on all folds

experiments.name: E3 with stronger L2 on compatibility matrices (1e-4 -> 1e-3)
experiments.decision: FINAL: better on 3/4 folds, lower NLL (1.44 vs 1.63)

experiments.name: Ensemble E3 + E1 (z-scored perm scores, w=0.2..0.4)
experiments.decision: rejected: lower on every fold (E1 overconfident)

experiments.name: Probe: token order (ordered vs shuffled content bigrams, naive Bayes)
experiments.decision: order carries little extra signal; order-aware encoder not pursued

findings: Filler n_ tokens are deterministic per message (full-token keys recur across groups as often as content keys) and carry weak signal.
~43% of validation last segments and ~52% of true outcomes recur (content-only) in other exchange groups; exact co-occurrence of (context, outcome) in other groups is ~72% precise.
Single-segment contexts are followed by an event outcome only 2.9% of the time vs 35.8% for two-segment contexts.
Bag-level bucket compatibility saturates around 50-55% exact permutation accuracy; because the metric is ~= exact permutation accuracy under optimal decoding, 0.70 requires ~70% exact accuracy.
final_chosen_approach: E3 permutation CRF (lambda 1e-3) trained on all training rows, memory features OOF by group for training rows and from the full training memory for test rows, MAP-permutation output.
